subject: Physics
stem: Consider a water tank shown in the figure. It has one wall at \(x = L\) and can be taken to be very wide in the \(z\) direction. When filled with a liquid of surface tension \(S\) and density \(\rho\), the liquid surface makes angle \(\theta_0\) (\(\theta_0 \ll 1\)) with the \(x\)-axis at \(x = L\). If \(y(x)\) is the height of the surface then the equation for \(y(x)\) is: (take \(\theta(x) = \sin\theta(x) = \tan\theta(x) = \frac{dy}{dx}\), \(g\) is the acceleration due to gravity)
solution: At point \(A\), curvature \(= \frac{1}{ROC} = \frac{\left|\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right|}{\left(1+\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2\right)^{3/2}} = \frac{d^2y}{dx^2}\) since \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \tan\theta \approx 0\). Excess pressure \(\Delta P = S \times\) curvature \(\Rightarrow \rho g y = S\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}\), so \(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \frac{\rho g y}{S}\).

subject: Physics
stem: A microscope has an objective of focal length 2 cm, eyepiece of focal length 4 cm and the tube length of 40 cm. If the distance of distinct vision of eye is 25 cm, the magnification in the microscope is
solution: \(m = \frac{L}{f_o} \times \frac{D}{f_e} = \frac{40}{2} \times \frac{25}{4} = 125\).

subtopic: Velocity Selector (Crossed E and B Fields)
stem: An electron (mass \(9 \times 10^{-31}\) kg and charge \(1.6 \times 10^{-19}\) C) moving with speed \(c/100\) (\(c\) = speed of light) is injected into a magnetic field \(\vec{B}\) of magnitude \(9 \times 10^{-4}\) T perpendicular to its direction of motion. We wish to apply an uniform electric field \(\vec{E}\) together with the magnetic field so that the electron does not deflect from its path. Then (speed of light \(c = 3 \times 10^8\) ms\(^{-1}\))
options: \(\vec{E}\) is perpendicular to \(\vec{B}\) and its magnitude is \(27 \times 10^4\) V m\(^{-1}\)
\(\vec{E}\) is perpendicular to \(\vec{B}\) and its magnitude is \(27 \times 10^2\) V m\(^{-1}\)
\(\vec{E}\) is parallel to \(\vec{B}\) and its magnitude is \(27 \times 10^2\) V m\(^{-1}\)
\(\vec{E}\) is parallel to \(\vec{B}\) and its magnitude is \(27 \times 10^4\) V m\(^{-1}\)
solution: For no deflection, \(\vec{F}_B = \vec{F}_E\). \(-e(\vec{v} \times \vec{B}) = -e\vec{E} \Rightarrow \vec{E} = \vec{v} \times \vec{B} \Rightarrow \vec{E} \perp \vec{B}\). \(E = vB = \frac{c}{100} \times 9 \times 10^{-4} = \frac{3 \times 10^8}{100} \times 9 \times 10^{-4} = 27 \times 10^2\) V m\(^{-1}\).

subject: Physics
stem: There are two inclined surfaces of equal length (\(L\)) and same angle of inclination 45\(^\circ\) with the horizontal. One of them is rough and the other is perfectly smooth. A given body takes 2 times as much time to slide down on rough surface than on the smooth surface. The coefficient of kinetic friction (\(\mu_k\)) between the object and the rough surface is close to
solution: \(t_{rough} = 2t_{smooth}\). \(a_{smooth} = g\sin\theta\), \(a_{rough} = g\sin\theta - \mu_k g\cos\theta\), and \(t \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{a}}\). So \(\frac{t_{rough}}{t_{smooth}} = \frac{\sqrt{\sin\theta}}{\sqrt{\sin\theta - \mu_k\cos\theta}} = 2\). Squaring: \(\frac{\sin\theta}{\sin\theta - \mu_k\cos\theta} = 4\). With \(\theta = 45^\circ\): \(\frac{1/\sqrt{2}}{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} - \mu_k\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}} = 4 \Rightarrow 1 - \mu_k = \frac{1}{4} \Rightarrow \mu_k = \frac{3}{4} = 0.75\).

subject: Physics
stem: The kinetic energies of two similar cars \(A\) and \(B\) are 100 J and 225 J respectively. On applying breaks, car \(A\) stops after 1000 m and car \(B\) stops after 1500 m. If \(F_A\) and \(F_B\) are the forces applied by the breaks on cars \(A\) and \(B\) respectively, then the ratio of \(\frac{F_A}{F_B}\) is
solution: By work-energy theorem, \(FS = \Delta K.E \Rightarrow -FS = k_f - k_i \Rightarrow FS = k_i - k_f\). So \(\frac{F_A}{F_B} = \frac{k_A}{k_B} \times \frac{S_B}{S_A} = \frac{100}{225} \times \frac{1500}{1000} = \frac{150}{225} = \frac{2}{3}\).

subject: Physics
stem: The current passing through the battery in the given circuit, is:
solution: The bridge A-B-C-D (arms 5\(\Omega\), 2.5\(\Omega\), 3\(\Omega\), 1.5\(\Omega\) with 6\(\Omega\) galvanometer arm) is a balanced Wheatstone bridge. Its equivalent \(R' = \frac{4 \times 8}{12} = \frac{8}{3}\,\Omega\). Redrawing: \(R_{eq} = \frac{8}{3} + \frac{1}{3} + 1.5 + 5.5 = 10\,\Omega\). \(i = \frac{V}{R_{eq}} = \frac{5}{10} = 0.5\) A.

stem: A bob of heavy mass \(m\) is suspended by a light string of length \(l\). The bob is given a horizontal velocity \(v_0\) as shown in figure. If the string gets slack at some point \(P\) making an angle \(\theta\) from the horizontal, the ratio of the speed \(v\) of the bob at point \(P\) to its initial speed \(v_0\) is:
solution: At point \(P\), string slack: \(mg\sin\theta = \frac{mv^2}{l}\) ...(1). By conservation of mechanical energy between \(Q\) and \(P\): \(\frac{1}{2}mv_0^2 = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 + mg(l + l\sin\theta)\). Putting \(gl = \frac{v^2}{\sin\theta}\) from (1): \(v_0^2 = v^2\left[3 + \frac{2}{\sin\theta}\right]\), so \(\frac{v}{v_0} = \left(\frac{\sin\theta}{3\sin\theta + 2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\).

subject: Physics
stem: The output (\(Y\)) of the given logic implementation is similar to the output of an/a _____ gate.
solution: The circuit gives \(Y_1 = \overline{A + B}\) (NOR) and \(Y_2 = \overline{A \cdot B}\) (NAND). \(Y = Y_1 \cdot Y_2 = \overline{A + B} \cdot \overline{A \cdot B} = \overline{(A+B) + A\cdot B} = \overline{A + B(1 + A)} = \overline{A + B}\), which is a NOR gate.

stem: The electric field in a plane electromagnetic wave is given by \(E_z = 60\cos(5x + 1.5 \times 10^9 t)\) V/m. Then expression for the corresponding magnetic field is (here subscripts denote the direction of the field):
solution: In an electromagnetic wave, \(E\) and \(B\) are in the same phase and \(B_0 = \frac{E_0}{c}\); their planes are perpendicular. So \(B_y = \frac{60}{c}\cos(5x + 1.5 \times 10^9 t) = \frac{60}{3 \times 10^8}\cos(5x + 1.5 \times 10^9 t) = 2 \times 10^{-7}\cos(5x + 1.5 \times 10^9 t)\,T\).

subject: Physics
stem: A ball of mass 0.5 kg is dropped from a height of 40 m. The ball hits the ground and rises to a height of 10 m. The impulse imparted to the ball during its collision with the ground is (Take \(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^2\))
solution: \(v_1 = \sqrt{2gh_1} = \sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 40} = \sqrt{784} = 28\) m s\(^{-1}\) (downward). \(v_2 = \sqrt{2gh_2} = \sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 10} = \sqrt{196} = 14\) m s\(^{-1}\) (upward). Impulse \(= \Delta\vec{p} = m(\vec{v}_2 - \vec{v}_1) = \frac{1}{2}(14 - (-28)) = 21\) NS.

subject: Physics
stem: \(AB\) is a part of an electrical circuit (see figure). The potential difference \(V_A - V_B\), at the instant when current \(i = 2\) A and is increasing at a rate of 1 amp/second is: (branch has a 1 H inductor, a 5 V cell and a 2\(\Omega\) resistor in series)
solution: Given \(i = 2\) A and \(\frac{di}{dt} = +1\) A/s. \(V_A - L\frac{di}{dt} - 5 - i \times 2 = V_B \Rightarrow V_A - 1 \times 1 - 5 - 2 \times 2 = V_B \Rightarrow V_A - V_B = 10\) volt.

subject: Physics
stem: A 2 amp current is flowing through two different small circular copper coils having radii ratio 1 : 2. The ratio of their respective magnetic moments will be
solution: Magnetic moment of a current carrying circular loop \(M = IA\). With \(I\) same, \(M \propto A\). \(\frac{M_1}{M_2} = \frac{A_1}{A_2} = \frac{\pi r_1^2}{\pi r_2^2} = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{4}\).

subject: Physics
stem: In a certain camera, a combination of four similar thin convex lenses are arranged axially in contact. Then the power of the combination and the total magnification in comparison to the power (\(p\)) and magnification (\(m\)) for each lens will be, respectively
solution: For series combination of lenses, \(p_{eff} = p_1 + p_2 + p_3 + p_4 = 4p\), and \(m_{eff} = m_1 \times m_2 \times m_3 \times m_4 = m^4\).

subject: Physics
stem: An oxygen cylinder of volume 30 litre has 18.20 moles of oxygen. After some oxygen is withdrawn from the cylinder, its gauge pressure drops to 11 atmospheric pressure at temperature 27\(^\circ\)C. The mass of the oxygen withdrawn from the cylinder is nearly equal to: [Given, \(R = \frac{100}{12}\) J mol\(^{-1}\)K\(^{-1}\), and molecular mass of O\(_2\) = 32, 1 atm pressure = \(1.01 \times 10^5\) N/m]
solution: Number of moles left \(n = \frac{PV}{RT} = \frac{12 \times 1.01 \times 10^5\,N/m^2 \times 30 \times 10^{-3}\,m^3}{\frac{100}{12} \times 300} = \frac{12 \times 1.01 \times 12}{10} = 14.54\) moles. Moles removed \(= 18.2 - 14.54 = 3.656\) moles. Mass removed \(= 3.656 \times 32 = 116.99\) g \(= 0.116\) kg.

stem: In some appropriate units, time (\(t\)) and position (\(x\)) relation of a moving particle is given by \(t = x^2 + x\). The acceleration of the particle is
solution: \(t = x^2 + x \Rightarrow \frac{dt}{dx} = 2x + 1\). \(v = \frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{1}{(2x+1)}\). \(\frac{dv}{dx} = \frac{-2}{(2x+1)^2}\). \(a = v\frac{dv}{dx} = \frac{1}{(2x+1)}\left[\frac{-2}{(2x+1)^2}\right] = -\frac{2}{(2x+1)^3}\).

chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
stem: The Sun rotates around its centre once in 27 days. What will be the period of revolution if the Sun were to expand to twice its present radius without any external influence? Assume the Sun to be a sphere of uniform density.
solution: Assuming the Sun to be a solid sphere, \(I = \frac{2}{5}mR^2\). Using conservation of angular momentum, \(I'\omega' = I\omega \Rightarrow \frac{2}{5}m(2R)^2 \times \frac{2\pi}{T'} = \frac{2}{5}mR^2 \times \frac{2\pi}{T} \Rightarrow T' = 4T = 4 \times 27 = 108\) days.

subject: Physics
stem: A model for quantized motion of an electron in a uniform magnetic field \(B\) states that the flux passing through the orbit of the electron is \(n(h/e)\) where \(n\) is an integer, \(h\) is Planck's constant and \(e\) is the magnitude of electron's charge. According to the model, the magnetic moment of an electron in its lowest energy state will be (\(m\) is the mass of the electron)
solution: Magnetic force provides centripetal force: \(evB = \frac{mv^2}{r} \Rightarrow v = \frac{eBr}{m}\). Flux \(\phi = BA \Rightarrow \frac{nh}{e} = B\pi r^2 \Rightarrow Br^2 = \frac{nh}{e\pi}\). Magnetic moment \(\mu = IA = \frac{e}{T}\pi r^2 = \frac{ev}{2\pi r}\pi r^2 = \frac{evr}{2} = \frac{1}{2}e \cdot \frac{eBr}{m} \cdot r = \frac{1}{2}e^2\frac{Br^2}{m} = \frac{1}{2}e^2\frac{nh}{e\pi m} = \frac{neh}{2\pi m}\). For \(n = 1\), \(\mu = \frac{eh}{2\pi m}\).

subject: Physics
stem: Three identical heat conducting rods are connected in series as shown in the figure. The rods on the sides have thermal conductivity \(2K\) while that in the middle has thermal conductivity \(K\). The left end of the combination is maintained at temperature \(3T\) and the right end at \(T\). The rods are thermally insulated from outside. In steady state, temperature at the left junction is \(T_1\) and that at the right junction is \(T_2\). The ratio \(T_1/T_2\) is
solution: In series, \(R_{eq} = \frac{l}{2KA} + \frac{l}{KA} + \frac{l}{2KA} = \frac{4l}{2KA} = \frac{2l}{KA}\). Rate of heat flow is same: \(\frac{3T - T_1}{R_1} = \frac{3T - T}{R_{eq}}\). \(\frac{(3T - T_1)2KA}{l} = \frac{(2T)KA}{2l} \Rightarrow 6T - 2T_1 = T \Rightarrow T_1 = \frac{5T}{2}\). Similarly \(\frac{T_2 - T}{R_3} = \frac{3T - T}{R_{eq}} \Rightarrow 2T_2 - 2T = T \Rightarrow T_2 = \frac{3T}{2}\). So \(\frac{T_1}{T_2} = \frac{5T \times 2}{2 \times 3T} = \frac{5}{3}\).

stem: Two cities \(X\) and \(Y\) are connected by a regular bus service with a bus leaving in either direction every \(T\) min. A girl is driving scooty with a speed of 60 km/h in the direction \(X\) to \(Y\) notices that a bus goes past her every 30 minutes in the direction of her motion, and every 10 minutes in the opposite direction. Choose the correct option for the period \(T\) of the bus service and the speed (assumed constant) of the buses.
solution: Let velocity of bus \(= v\) km/hr. \(X \to Y\): relative velocity \(= (v - 60)\), distance between 2 consecutive buses \(= vT\), so \((v - 60)30 = vT\) ...(i). \(Y \to X\): \((v + 60)10 = vT\) ...(ii). Equating: \((v - 60)30 = (v + 60)10 \Rightarrow v = 120\) km/hr, and \(T = 15\) min.

chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
stem: A uniform rod of mass 20 kg and length 5 m leans against a smooth vertical wall making an angle of 60\(^\circ\) with it. The other end rests on a rough horizontal floor. The friction force that the floor exerts on the rod is (Take \(g = 10\) m/s\(^2\))
solution: The rod makes 60\(^\circ\) with the wall, i.e. 30\(^\circ\) with the floor (\(\theta = 30^\circ\)). For translational equilibrium: \(N_1 = Mg\), \(N_2 = f\). For rotational equilibrium (torque about the floor end \(A\)): \(Mg\frac{L}{2}\cos\theta = N_2 L\sin\theta \Rightarrow \frac{Mg}{2}\cot\theta = N_2 = f\). \(f = \frac{Mg}{2}\cot 30^\circ = \frac{200}{2}\sqrt{3} = 100\sqrt{3}\) N.

subject: Physics
stem: In an oscillating spring mass system, a spring is connected to a box filled with sand. As the box oscillates, sand leaks slowly out of the box vertically so that the average frequency \(\omega(t)\) and average amplitude \(A(t)\) of the system change with time \(t\). Which one of the following options schematically depicts these changes correctly?
solution: At any point of time, \(T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{m}{k}}\). Here \(m\) is decreasing, so time period \(T\) decreases. Since \(\omega = \frac{2\pi}{T}\), as mass leaks, \(\omega\) increases. Also \(mg = kx_0\), so equilibrium length \(x_0 = \frac{mg}{k}\) decreases as \(m\) decreases, hence the amplitude also decreases. So \(\omega(t)\) increases and \(A(t)\) decreases.

subject: Physics
stem: A balloon is made of a material of surface tension \(S\) and its inflation outlet (from where gas is filled in it) has small area \(A\). It is filled with a gas of density \(\rho\) and takes a spherical shape of radius \(R\). When the gas is allowed to flow freely out of it, its radius \(r\) changes from \(R\) to 0 (zero) in time \(T\). If the speed \(v(r)\) of gas coming out of the balloon depends on \(r\) as \(r^a\) and \(T \propto S^\alpha \rho^\gamma R^\delta\) (with an additional \(A^\beta\) factor) then
solution: \(T \propto S^\alpha A^\beta \rho^\gamma R^\delta\). Dimensionally \(M^0L^0T^1 = K(MT^{-2})^\alpha (L^2)^\beta (ML^{-3})^\gamma L^\delta = K M^{\alpha+\gamma}L^{2\beta - 3\gamma + \delta}T^{-2\alpha}\). So \(-2\alpha = 1 \Rightarrow \alpha = -\frac{1}{2}\); \(\alpha + \gamma = 0 \Rightarrow \gamma = \frac{1}{2}\); \(2\beta - 3\gamma + \delta = 0\). With \(\beta = -1\): \(2(-1) - \frac{3}{2} + \delta = 0 \Rightarrow \delta = \frac{7}{2}\).

subject: Physics
stem: Consider the diameter of a spherical object being measured with the help of a Vernier callipers. Suppose its 10 Vernier Scale Divisions (V.S.D.) are equal to its 9 Main Scale Divisions (M.S.D.). The least division in the M.S. is 0.1 cm and the zero of V.S. is at \(x = 0.1\) cm when the jaws of Vernier callipers are closed. If the main scale reading for the diameter is \(M = 5\) cm and the number of coinciding vernier division is 8, the measured diameter after zero error correction, is
solution: Least count \(= 1\,MSD - 1\,VSD = 1\,MSD - \frac{9}{10}MSD = \frac{1}{10}MSD = \frac{1}{10} \times 0.1 = 0.01\) cm. Zero error \(= +0.1\) cm. Main scale reading \(= 5\) cm, Vernier scale reading \(= 8 \times 0.01 = 0.08\) cm. Final diameter \(= 5 + 0.08 - 0.1 = 4.98\) cm.

subject: Physics
stem: A parallel plate capacitor made of circular plates is being charged such that the surface charge density on its plates is increasing at a constant rate with time. The magnetic field arising due to displacement current is:
options: Constant between the plates and zero outside the plates
Non-zero everywhere with maximum at the imaginary cylindrical surface connecting peripheries of the plates
Zero between the plates and non-zero outside
solution: Let surface charge density \(\sigma = \frac{q}{A}\). Given \(\frac{d\sigma}{dt}\) = constant, so \(\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{q}{A}\right)\) = constant \(\Rightarrow \frac{i}{A}\) = constant, i.e. displacement current is constant. The system acts like a cylindrical wire: \(B\) increases linearly with \(r\) inside, reaching maximum at the periphery (\(r = R\)) and then decreasing as \(1/r\) outside.

subject: Physics
stem: An unpolarized light beam travelling in air is incident on a medium of refractive index 1.73 at Brewster's angle. Then
options: Reflected light is completely polarized and the angle of reflection is close to 60\(^\circ\)
Reflected light is partially polarized and the angle of reflection is close to 30\(^\circ\)
Both reflected and transmitted light are perfectly polarized with angles of reflection and refraction close to 60\(^\circ\) and 30\(^\circ\), respectively
Transmitted light is completely polarized with angle of refraction close to 30\(^\circ\)
solution: Using Brewster's law, \(\mu = \tan\theta_P \Rightarrow 1.73 = \tan\theta_P \Rightarrow \sqrt{3} = \tan\theta_P \Rightarrow \theta_P = 60^\circ\). At this polarising angle, the reflected light is perfectly (completely) polarised with angle of reflection close to 60\(^\circ\) and the transmitted light is partially polarised.

subject: Physics
stem: Two identical charged conducting spheres \(A\) and \(B\) have their centres separated by a certain distance. Charge on each sphere is \(q\) and the force of repulsion between them is \(F\). A third identical uncharged conducting sphere is brought in contact with sphere \(A\) first and then with \(B\) and finally removed from both. New force of repulsion between spheres \(A\) and \(B\) (Radii of \(A\) and \(B\) are negligible compared to the distance of separation so that for calculating force between them they can be considered as point charges) is best given as:
solution: Initially \(F = \frac{Kqq}{r^2}\). After touching \(A\) (uncharged sphere), \(A\) has \(\frac{q}{2}\). Then touching \(B\): charge shared between \(\frac{q}{2}\) and \(q\) gives each \(\frac{3q}{4}\). So \(A\) has \(\frac{q}{2}\), \(B\) has \(\frac{3q}{4}\). \(F' = \frac{K \cdot \frac{q}{2} \cdot \frac{3q}{4}}{r^2} = \frac{3F}{8}\).

stem: A particle of mass \(m\) is moving around the origin with a constant force \(F\) pulling it towards the origin. If Bohr model is used to describe its motion, the radius of the \(n^{th}\) orbit and the particle's speed \(v\) in the orbit depend on \(n\) as
solution: Given force is constant. \(F = \frac{mv^2}{r} \Rightarrow \frac{v^2}{r}\) = constant \(\Rightarrow r \propto v^2\) ...(1). Bohr quantization: \(L = mvr = \frac{nh}{2\pi}\) ...(2). Solving (1) and (2): \(v \propto n^{1/3}\) and \(r \propto n^{2/3}\).

subject: Physics
stem: The radius of Martian orbit around the Sun is about 4 times the radius of the orbit of Mercury. The Martian year is 687 Earth days. Then which of the following is the length of 1 year on Mercury?
solution: Applying Kepler's 3rd law: \(T^2 \propto R^3\). Radius of Martian orbit \(R' = 4R\). \(\left(\frac{T'}{T}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{R'}{R}\right)^3 = \left(\frac{4R}{R}\right)^3 = 4^3 = 64 \Rightarrow \frac{T'}{T} = 8\). Length of 1 year on Mercury \(= T = \frac{T'}{8} = \frac{687}{8} = 85.88\) days \(\approx 88\) earth days.

subject: Physics
stem: A body weighs 48 N on the surface of the earth. The gravitational force experienced by the body due to the earth at a height equal to one-third the radius of the earth from its surface is:
solution: \(W = mg\), \(g = \frac{GM}{R^2}\), \(g_h = \frac{GM}{(R+h)^2}\). With \(h = \frac{R}{3}\): \(\frac{W_h}{W} = \frac{R^2}{(R+h)^2} = \frac{R^2}{\left(\frac{4R}{3}\right)^2} = \frac{9}{16}\). So \(W_h = \frac{9}{16} \times 48 = 27\) N.

subject: Physics
stem: A wire of resistance \(R\) is cut into 8 equal pieces. From these pieces two equivalent resistances are made by adding four of these together in parallel. Then these two sets are added in series. The net effective resistance of the combination is:
solution: After cutting into 8 equal pieces, resistance of each piece \(R' = \frac{R}{8}\). Each set has 4 pieces in parallel: \(R'' = \frac{R'}{4} = \frac{R}{32}\). Both sets in series: \(R_{eq} = R'' + R'' = 2 \times \frac{R}{32} = \frac{R}{16}\).

stem: An electric dipole with dipole moment \(5 \times 10^{-6}\) Cm is aligned with the direction of a uniform electric field of magnitude \(4 \times 10^5\) N/C. The dipole is then rotated through an angle of 60\(^\circ\) with respect to the electric field. The change in the potential energy of the dipole is:
solution: Given \(|\vec{P}| = 5 \times 10^{-6}\) Cm, \(|\vec{E}| = 4 \times 10^5\) N/C, \(\theta_i = 0^\circ\) and \(\theta_f = 60^\circ\). \(\Delta U = U_f - U_i = -PE\cos\theta_f + PE\cos\theta_i = PE[\cos\theta_i - \cos\theta_f] = 5 \times 10^{-6} \times 4 \times 10^5\left[1 - \frac{1}{2}\right] = 10 \times 10^{-6} \times 10^5 = 1\) J.

stem: A constant voltage of 50 V is maintained between the points \(A\) and \(B\) of the circuit shown in the figure. The current through the branch \(CD\) of the circuit is:
solution: \(R_{AB} = (1\Omega \| 3\Omega)\) in series with \((2\Omega \| 4\Omega) = \frac{3 \times 1}{3+1} + \frac{2 \times 4}{2+4} = \frac{3}{4} + \frac{8}{6} = \frac{9+16}{12} = \frac{25}{12}\,\Omega\). Total current \(I = \frac{50}{25/12} = 24\) A. \(I_{1\Omega} = \frac{3}{4} \times 24 = 18\) A, \(I_{2\Omega} = \frac{4}{6} \times 24 = 16\) A. Using junction rule at \(C\): \(I_{CD} = 18 - 16 = 2\) A (from \(C\) to \(D\)).

subtopic: De-Broglie Wavelength of Photon and Electron
stem: A photon and an electron (mass \(m\)) have the same energy \(E\). The ratio \((\lambda_{photon}/\lambda_{electron})\) of their de Broglie wavelengths is: (\(c\) is the speed of light)
solution: For photon, \(E = \frac{hc}{\lambda_{ph}} \Rightarrow \lambda_{ph} = \frac{hc}{E}\). For electron, \(E = \frac{p^2}{2m} = \left(\frac{h}{\lambda_e}\right)^2 \times \frac{1}{2m} \Rightarrow \lambda_e = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mE}}\). So \(\frac{\lambda_{ph}}{\lambda_e} = \frac{hc/E}{h/\sqrt{2mE}} = c\sqrt{\frac{2m}{E}}\).

stem: Which of the following options represent the variation of photoelectric current with property of light shown on the \(x\)-axis? A. Photoelectric current increasing linearly through origin vs Intensity of light. B. Photoelectric current constant (horizontal line) vs Intensity of light. C. Photoelectric current increasing linearly through origin vs Frequency of light. D. Photoelectric current increasing linearly (with a positive x-intercept) vs Frequency of light.
solution: Photoelectric current is directly proportional to intensity of light. So the correct graph is A only (photoelectric current increasing linearly with intensity through the origin).

chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
subtopic: Moment of Inertia of a Cavity
stem: A sphere of radius \(R\) is cut from a larger solid sphere of radius \(2R\) as shown in the figure. The ratio of the moment of inertia of the smaller sphere to that of the rest part of the sphere about the \(Y\)-axis is:
solution: For the larger solid sphere about the diameter \(Y\)-axis, \(I_{whole} = \frac{2}{5}M(2R)^2 = \frac{8}{5}MR^2\). Density uniform \(\Rightarrow M' = \frac{M}{8}\) (smaller sphere mass). Using parallel axis theorem for the smaller sphere (its centre at distance \(R\) from \(Y\)-axis): \(I' = I_{cm} + M'R^2 = \frac{2}{5}\frac{MR^2}{8} + \frac{MR^2}{8} = \frac{7}{40}MR^2\). Ratio \(= \frac{I_{smaller}}{I_{remaining}} = \frac{I'}{I_{whole} - I'} = \frac{\frac{7}{40}MR^2}{\left(\frac{8}{5} - \frac{7}{40}\right)MR^2} = \frac{7}{64 - 7} = \frac{7}{57}\).

subject: Physics
stem: A full wave rectifier circuit with diodes (\(D_1\)) and (\(D_2\)) is shown in the figure. If input supply voltage \(V_{in} = 220\sin(100\pi t)\) volt, then at \(t = 15\) msec
options: \(D_1\) is forward biased, \(D_2\) is reverse biased
\(D_1\) is reverse biased, \(D_2\) is forward biased
solution: \(V_{in} = 220\sin(100\pi t)\) volt. \(t = 15\) ms \(= 0.015\) s, \(\omega = 100\pi\), so \(\frac{2\pi}{T} = 100\pi \Rightarrow T = \frac{1}{50} = 0.02\) s. Thus \(t = \frac{3T}{4}\), i.e. negative half cycle. So the negative half cycle is fed to the circuit, making \(D_1\) reverse biased and \(D_2\) forward biased.

subject: Physics
stem: Two gases \(A\) and \(B\) are filled at the same pressure in separate cylinders with movable pistons of radius \(r_A\) and \(r_B\), respectively. On supplying an equal amount of heat to both the systems reversibly under constant pressure, the pistons of gas \(A\) and \(B\) are displaced by 16 cm and 9 cm, respectively. If the change in their internal energy is the same, then the ratio \(\frac{r_A}{r_B}\) is equal to
solution: Using first law: \(\Delta Q = \Delta U + P\Delta V\). \(\Delta Q\) same, \(\Delta U\) same, so \(W_A = W_B \Rightarrow (P\Delta V)_A = (P\Delta V)_B\). \(P\) same, so \(A_A d_A = A_B d_B\), i.e. \(\pi r_A^2 d_A = \pi r_B^2 d_B\). \(\frac{r_A}{r_B} = \left(\frac{d_B}{d_A}\right)^{1/2} = \left(\frac{9}{16}\right)^{1/2} = \frac{3}{4}\).

subject: Physics
stem: A physical quantity \(P\) is related to four observations \(a, b, c\) and \(d\) as follows: \(P = a^3 b^2 / c\sqrt{d}\). The percentage errors of measurement in \(a, b, c\) and \(d\) are 1%, 3%, 2%, and 4% respectively. The percentage error in the quantity \(P\) is
solution: Maximum % error in \(P = \frac{\Delta P}{P} \times 100 = 3\left(\frac{\Delta a}{a} \times 100\right) + 2\left(\frac{\Delta b}{b} \times 100\right) + \left(\frac{\Delta c}{c} \times 100\right) + \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\Delta d}{d} \times 100\right) = 3(1) + 2(3) + (2) + \frac{1}{2}(4) = 13\%\).

subject: Physics
stem: The intensity of transmitted light when a polaroid sheet, placed between two crossed polaroids at 22.5\(^\circ\) from the polarization axis of one of the polaroids, is (\(I_0\) is the intensity of polarised light after passing through the first polaroid):
solution: \(I_1 = I_0\cos^2\left(\frac{45}{2}\right)\). \(I_2 = I_1\cos^2\left(90 - \frac{45}{2}\right) = I_0\cos^2\left(\frac{45}{2}\right)\sin^2\left(\frac{45}{2}\right) = \frac{I_0}{4}\left(4\cos^2\left(\frac{45}{2}\right)\sin^2\left(\frac{45}{2}\right)\right) = \frac{I_0}{4}\sin^2 45^\circ = \frac{I_0}{8}\).

subject: Physics
stem: Two identical point masses \(P\) and \(Q\), suspended from two separate massless springs of spring constants \(k_1\) and \(k_2\), respectively, oscillate vertically. If their maximum speeds are the same, the ratio \((A_Q/A_P)\) of the amplitude \(A_Q\) of mass \(Q\) to the amplitude \(A_P\) of mass \(P\) is
solution: Maximum velocity \(V = A\omega\). \(v_P = v_Q \Rightarrow A_P\omega_P = A_Q\omega_Q\). \(\frac{A_Q}{A_P} = \frac{\omega_P}{\omega_Q}\) where \(\omega = \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}\). \(= \sqrt{\frac{k_P}{m_P}\frac{m_Q}{k_Q}} = \sqrt{\frac{k_1}{k_2}}\) (since \(m_P = m_Q\)).

subject: Physics
stem: A pipe open at both ends has a fundamental frequency \(f\) in air. The pipe is now dipped vertically in a water drum to half of its length. The fundamental frequency of the air column is now equal to:
solution: Fundamental frequency of an open pipe (open at both ends): \(f = \frac{v}{2L}\) ...(i). When immersed in water to half its length, the open pipe behaves as a closed pipe of length \(\frac{L}{2}\): \(f' = \frac{v}{4(L/2)} = \frac{v}{2L}\) ...(ii). So \(f = f'\).
